problem_description.description: Neko is playing with his toys on the backyard of Aki's house. Aki decided to play a prank on him, by secretly putting catnip into Neko's toys. Unfortunately, he went overboard and put an entire bag of catnip into the toys...It took Neko an entire day to turn back to normal. Neko reported to Aki that he saw a lot of weird things, including a trie of all correct bracket sequences of length $$$2n$$$.The definition of correct bracket sequence is as follows:  The empty sequence is a correct bracket sequence,  If $$$s$$$ is a correct bracket sequence, then $$$(\,s\,)$$$ is a correct bracket sequence,  If $$$s$$$ and $$$t$$$ are a correct bracket sequence, then $$$st$$$ is also a correct bracket sequence. For example, the strings "(())", "()()" form a correct bracket sequence, while ")(" and "((" not.Aki then came up with an interesting problem: What is the size of the maximum matching (the largest set of edges such that there are no two edges with a common vertex) in this trie? Since the answer can be quite large, print it modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 1000$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Print exactly one integer — the size of the maximum matching in the trie. Since the answer can be quite large, print it modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe pictures below illustrate tries in the first two examples (for clarity, the round brackets are replaced with angle brackets). The maximum matching is highlighted with blue.

problem_description.description: Alice has got addicted to a game called Sirtet recently.In Sirtet, player is given an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. Initially $$$a_{i,j}$$$ cubes are stacked up in the cell $$$(i,j)$$$. Two cells are called adjacent if they share a side. Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer, representing the desired answer modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the only initial grid that satisfies the requirements is $$$a_{1,1}=a_{2,1}=a_{1,2}=a_{2,2}=1$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$1$$$.In the second sample, initial grids that satisfy the requirements are $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=1$$$ and $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=2$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$2$$$.

    res = 1
    while exp > 0:

        base = (base * base) % MOD
        exp >>= 1
    return res

problem_description.description: Alice has got addicted to a game called Sirtet recently.In Sirtet, player is given an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. Initially $$$a_{i,j}$$$ cubes are stacked up in the cell $$$(i,j)$$$. Two cells are called adjacent if they share a side. Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer, representing the desired answer modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the only initial grid that satisfies the requirements is $$$a_{1,1}=a_{2,1}=a_{1,2}=a_{2,2}=1$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$1$$$.In the second sample, initial grids that satisfy the requirements are $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=1$$$ and $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=2$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$2$$$.

import sys
import math

MOD = 998244353

def mod_pow(base, exp, mod):
    """Compute (base^exp) % mod using fast exponentiation"""
    result = 1
    base = base % mod
    while exp > 0:
        if exp & 1:
            result = (result * base) % mod
        exp >>= 1
        base = (base * base) % mod
    return result

def main():

        n = int(data[idx])
        m = int(data[idx + 1])
        l = int(data[idx + 2])
        r = int(data[idx + 3])
        idx += 4
        
        k = r - l
        even = k // 2 + 1
        odd = (k + 1) // 2
        
        if (n * m) % 2 == 1:
            base = k + 1
            exp = n * m
            result = mod_pow(base, exp, MOD)
            out_lines.append(str(result))
        else:
            base1 = even + odd
            base2 = even - odd
            exp = n * m
            
            temp1 = mod_pow(base1, exp, MOD)
            temp2 = mod_pow(base2, exp, MOD)
            
            sum_val = (temp1 + temp2) % MOD
            half = (MOD + 1) // 2
            result = (sum_val * half) % MOD
            out_lines.append(str(result))
    
    print('\n'.join(out_lines))

problem_description.description: Alice has got addicted to a game called Sirtet recently.In Sirtet, player is given an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. Initially $$$a_{i,j}$$$ cubes are stacked up in the cell $$$(i,j)$$$. Two cells are called adjacent if they share a side. Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer, representing the desired answer modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the only initial grid that satisfies the requirements is $$$a_{1,1}=a_{2,1}=a_{1,2}=a_{2,2}=1$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$1$$$.In the second sample, initial grids that satisfy the requirements are $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=1$$$ and $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=2$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$2$$$.

    result = 1
    base %= MOD
    while exp > 0:
        if (exp & 1) == 1:

        base = (base * base) % MOD
        exp >>= 1
    return result

def mod_inverse(x):
    return mod_pow(x, MOD - 2)

Initially $$$a_{i,j}$$$ cubes are stacked up in the cell $$$(i,j)$$$. Two cells are called adjacent if they share a side. Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).

import sys

def mod_pow(b, e, m):
    b %= m
    res = 1
    while e > 0:
        if (e & 1) == 1:
            res = (res * b) % m
        b = (b * b) % m
        e >>= 1
    return res

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read
    data = input().split()
    
    n = int(data[0])
    m = int(data[1])
    k = n * m
    l = int(data[2])
    r = int(data[3])
    length = r - l + 1
    MOD = 998244353

    if k % 2 == 1:
        ans = mod_pow(length, k, MOD)
    else:
        t1 = mod_pow(length, k, MOD)
        t2 = mod_pow(length % 2, k, MOD)
        ans = (t1 + t2) % MOD
        ans = ans * mod_pow(2, MOD - 2, MOD) % MOD
    
    print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: Alice has got addicted to a game called Sirtet recently.In Sirtet, player is given an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. Initially $$$a_{i,j}$$$ cubes are stacked up in the cell $$$(i,j)$$$. Two cells are called adjacent if they share a side. Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer, representing the desired answer modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the only initial grid that satisfies the requirements is $$$a_{1,1}=a_{2,1}=a_{1,2}=a_{2,2}=1$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$1$$$.In the second sample, initial grids that satisfy the requirements are $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=1$$$ and $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=2$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$2$$$.

import sys
import io

class InputReader:
    def __init__(self, stream):
        self.stream = stream
        self.buf = bytearray(1024)
        self.curChar = 0
        self.numChars = 0

    def read(self):
        if self.curChar >= self.numChars:
            self.curChar = 0
            self.numChars = self.stream.readinto(self.buf)
            if self.numChars <= 0:
                return -1
        c = self.buf[self.curChar]
        self.curChar += 1
        return c

    def read_string(self):
        c = self.read()
        while self.is_space_char(c):
            c = self.read()
        res = bytearray()
        while not self.is_space_char(c):
            res.append(c)
            c = self.read()
        return res.decode('ascii')

    def read_string_len(self, L):
        c = self.read()
        while self.is_space_char(c):
            c = self.read()
        res = bytearray(L)
        i = 0
        while not self.is_space_char(c) and i < L:
            res[i] = c
            i += 1
            c = self.read()
        return res[:i].decode('ascii')

    def read_int(self):
        c = self.read()
        neg = False
        while self.is_space_char(c):
            c = self.read()
        d = c
        if d == ord('-'):
            neg = True
            c = self.read()
        res = 0
        while not self.is_space_char(c):
            res = res * 10 + (c - ord('0'))
            c = self.read()
        if neg:
            return -res
        return res

    def read_long(self):
        c = self.read()
        neg = False
        while self.is_space_char(c):
            c = self.read()
        d = c
        if d == ord('-'):
            neg = True
            c = self.read()
        res = 0
        while not self.is_space_char(c):
            res = res * 10 + (c - ord('0'))
            c = self.read()
        if neg:
            return -res
        return res

    def is_space_char(self, c):
        return c in (ord(' '), ord('\n'), ord('\r'), ord('\t'), -1)


def power_mod(b, e, m):
    x = 1
    while e > 0:
        if e % 2 == 1:
            x = (b * x) % m
        b = (b * b) % m
        e = e // 2
    return x


def process():
    out = sys.stdout
    reader = InputReader(sys.stdin)

    n = reader.read_long()
    m = reader.read_long()
    L = reader.read_int()
    R = reader.read_int()
    
    mod = 998244353
    inv2 = power_mod(2, mod - 2, mod)
    
    ans = 0
    nm = n * m
    
    diff = R - L + 1
    p1 = diff // 2
    p2 = diff - p1
    
    if nm % 2 == 1:
        ans = power_mod(diff, nm, mod)
    else:
        pp1 = diff
        pp2 = abs(p1 - p2)
        
        opt1 = power_mod(pp1, nm, mod)
        opt2 = power_mod(pp2, nm, mod)
        opt = (opt1 + opt2) % mod
        opt = (opt * inv2) % mod
        ans = opt
    
    out.write(str(ans) + "\n")
    out.flush()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    process()

            base = (base * base) % mod;
            exp >>= 1;

problem_description.description: Alice has got addicted to a game called Sirtet recently.In Sirtet, player is given an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. Initially $$$a_{i,j}$$$ cubes are stacked up in the cell $$$(i,j)$$$. Two cells are called adjacent if they share a side. Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer, representing the desired answer modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the only initial grid that satisfies the requirements is $$$a_{1,1}=a_{2,1}=a_{1,2}=a_{2,2}=1$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$1$$$.In the second sample, initial grids that satisfy the requirements are $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=1$$$ and $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=2$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$2$$$.

import sys

MOD = 998244353

def identity_matrix(n):
    identity = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        identity[i][i] = 1
    return identity

def multiply_matrices(a, b):
    n = len(a)
    m = len(b[0])
    k = len(a[0])
    product = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(m):
            total = 0
            for p in range(k):
                total = (total + (a[i][p] % MOD) * (b[p][j] % MOD)) % MOD
            product[i][j] = total
    return product

def matrix_power(base, exponent):
    size = len(base)
    result = identity_matrix(size)
    while exponent > 0:
        if exponent & 1:
            result = multiply_matrices(result, base)
        base = multiply_matrices(base, base)
        exponent >>= 1
    return result

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    m = int(data[1])
    L = int(data[2])
    R = int(data[3])
    range_val = R - L

    evenCount, oddCount = 0, 0
    if range_val % 2 == 1:
        evenCount = (range_val + 1) // 2
        oddCount = (range_val + 1) // 2
    else:
        evenCount = range_val // 2
        oddCount = range_val // 2
        if L % 2 == 1:
            oddCount += 1
        else:
            evenCount += 1

    baseMatrix = [[evenCount, oddCount], [oddCount, evenCount]]
    resultMatrix = matrix_power(baseMatrix, n * m)
    answer = resultMatrix[0][0]
    if (n * m) % 2 == 1:
        answer = (answer + resultMatrix[0][1]) % MOD
    print(answer)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys

MOD = 998244353

def matrix_power_iterative(base, exp):
    size = len(base)
    result = [[1 if i == j else 0 for j in range(size)] for i in range(size)]
    
    while exp > 0:
        if exp & 1:
            result = multiply(result, base)
        base = multiply(base, base)
        exp >>= 1
    return result

def multiply(a, b):
    n = len(a)
    m = len(b[0])
    k = len(a[0])
    res = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(m):
            val = 0
            for p in range(k):
                val = (val + (a[i][p] % MOD) * (b[p][j] % MOD)) % MOD
            res[i][j] = val
    return res

def main():
    input_line = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
    input_parts = input_line.split(" ")
    n = int(input_parts[0])
    m = int(input_parts[1])
    L = int(input_parts[2])
    R = int(input_parts[3])
    range_val = R - L
    
    evenCount, oddCount = 0, 0
    if range_val % 2 == 1:
        evenCount = (range_val + 1) // 2
        oddCount = (range_val + 1) // 2
    else:
        evenCount = oddCount = range_val // 2
        if L % 2 == 1:
            oddCount += 1
        else:
            evenCount += 1
    
    base = [[evenCount, oddCount], [oddCount, evenCount]]
    powered = matrix_power_iterative(base, n * m)
    ans = powered[0][0]
    if (n * m) % 2 == 1:
        ans = (ans + powered[0][1]) % MOD
    print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: Alice has got addicted to a game called Sirtet recently.In Sirtet, player is given an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. Initially $$$a_{i,j}$$$ cubes are stacked up in the cell $$$(i,j)$$$. Two cells are called adjacent if they share a side. Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer, representing the desired answer modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the only initial grid that satisfies the requirements is $$$a_{1,1}=a_{2,1}=a_{1,2}=a_{2,2}=1$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$1$$$.In the second sample, initial grids that satisfy the requirements are $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=1$$$ and $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=2$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$2$$$.

import sys
from math import pow

def main():
    MOD = 998244353
    
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    m = int(data[1])
    L = int(data[2])
    R = int(data[3])
    
    k = R - L + 1
    
    if (n * m) % 2 == 1:
        exp = n * m
        base = k
        result = pow(base, exp, MOD)
        print(result)
    else:
        e = R // 2 - (L - 1) // 2
        o = k - e
        E = e
        O = o
        exp = n * m
        
        a = pow(E + O, exp, MOD)
        b = pow(E - O, exp, MOD)
        
        result = (a + b) * (MOD + 1) // 2 % MOD
        print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys
from math import pow

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.readline
    st = input().split()
    n = int(st[0])
    m = int(st[1])
    L = int(st[2])
    R = int(st[3])
    MOD = 998244353
    k = R - L + 1

    if (n * m) & 1 == 1:
        base = k
        exp = n * m
        print(pow(base, exp, MOD))
    else:
        even = (R // 2) - ((L - 1) // 2)
        odd = k - even
        E = even
        O = odd
        exp = n * m
        term1 = pow(E + O, exp, MOD)
        term2 = pow(E - O, exp, MOD)
        ans = (term1 + term2) * (MOD + 1) // 2 % MOD
        print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        even = (R // 2) - ((L - 1) // 2)
        odd = k - even
        E = even
        O = odd
        exp = n * m

        # Since (MOD + 1) // 2 is the modular inverse of 2 mod MOD

        result = (A + B) * inv2 % MOD
        print(result)

import sys

def main():
    MOD = 998244353
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    m = int(data[1])
    L = int(data[2])
    R = int(data[3])
    k = R - L + 1
    
    if (n * m) & 1 == 1:
        base = k
        exp = n * m
        result = pow(base, exp, MOD)
        print(result)
    else:
        evens = (R >> 1) - ((L - 1) >> 1)
        odds = k - evens
        E = evens
        O = odds
        exp = n * m
        sum_val = E + O
        diff = E - O
        term1 = pow(sum_val, exp, MOD)
        term2 = pow(diff, exp, MOD)
        numerator = (term1 + term2) * (MOD + 1)
        result = (numerator // 2) % MOD
        print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: Alice has got addicted to a game called Sirtet recently.In Sirtet, player is given an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. Initially $$$a_{i,j}$$$ cubes are stacked up in the cell $$$(i,j)$$$. Two cells are called adjacent if they share a side. Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer, representing the desired answer modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the only initial grid that satisfies the requirements is $$$a_{1,1}=a_{2,1}=a_{1,2}=a_{2,2}=1$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$1$$$.In the second sample, initial grids that satisfy the requirements are $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=1$$$ and $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=2$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$2$$$.

            b -= 1
        a = (a * a) % mod
        b //= 2
    return res

import sys
from collections import defaultdict

MOD = 998244353

def mod_pow(base, exp):
    res = 1
    base %= MOD
    while exp > 0:
        if exp & 1:
            res = (res * base) % MOD
        base = (base * base) % MOD
        exp >>= 1
    return res

even = 0
odd = 0
memo0 = {}
memo1 = {}

def f(n, p):
    global even, odd, memo0, memo1, MOD
    if p == 0:
        if n in memo0:
            return memo0[n]
        if n == 1:
            val = even
        elif n == 2:
            val = (even * even % MOD + odd * odd % MOD) % MOD
        else:
            h = n // 2
            rem = n - h
            a1 = f(h, 0)
            a2 = f(rem, 0)
            b1 = f(h, 1)
            b2 = f(rem, 1)
            val = (a1 * a2 % MOD + b1 * b2 % MOD) % MOD
        memo0[n] = val
        return val
    else:
        if n in memo1:
            return memo1[n]
        if n == 1:
            val = odd
        elif n == 2:
            val = (even * odd % MOD + odd * even % MOD) % MOD
        else:
            h = n // 2
            rem = n - h
            a1 = f(h, 0)
            a2 = f(rem, 1)
            b1 = f(h, 1)
            b2 = f(rem, 0)
            val = (a1 * a2 % MOD + b1 * b2 % MOD) % MOD
        memo1[n] = val
        return val

def solve():

        if (r - l) % 2 == 0 and l % 2 == 0:

        odd = cnt - even
        memo0.clear()

        print(f(sz, 0))

        print(mod_pow(r - l + 1, sz))

def main():
    t = 1
    for _ in range(t):
        solve()

problem_description.description: Alice has got addicted to a game called Sirtet recently.In Sirtet, player is given an $$$n \times m$$$ grid. Initially $$$a_{i,j}$$$ cubes are stacked up in the cell $$$(i,j)$$$. Two cells are called adjacent if they share a side. Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer, representing the desired answer modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the only initial grid that satisfies the requirements is $$$a_{1,1}=a_{2,1}=a_{1,2}=a_{2,2}=1$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$1$$$.In the second sample, initial grids that satisfy the requirements are $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=1$$$ and $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=2$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$2$$$.

Player can perform the following operations:   stack up one cube in two adjacent cells;  stack up two cubes in one cell. Cubes mentioned above are identical in height.Here is an illustration of the game. States on the right are obtained by performing one of the above operations on the state on the left, and grey cubes are added due to the operation.  Player's goal is to make the height of all cells the same (i.e. so that each cell has the same number of cubes in it) using above operations. Alice, however, has found out that on some starting grids she may never reach the goal no matter what strategy she uses. Thus, she is wondering the number of initial grids such that   $$$L \le a_{i,j} \le R$$$ for all $$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le m$$$;  player can reach the goal using above operations. Please help Alice with it. Notice that the answer might be large, please output the desired value modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The only line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$L$$$ and $$$R$$$ ($$$1\le n,m,L,R \le 10^9$$$, $$$L \le R$$$, $$$n \cdot m \ge 2$$$).
problem_description.output_spec: Output one integer, representing the desired answer modulo $$$998,244,353$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the only initial grid that satisfies the requirements is $$$a_{1,1}=a_{2,1}=a_{1,2}=a_{2,2}=1$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$1$$$.In the second sample, initial grids that satisfy the requirements are $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=1$$$ and $$$a_{1,1}=a_{1,2}=2$$$. Thus the answer should be $$$2$$$.

import sys

MOD = 998244353

def power(x, y, p):
    res = 1
    x = x % p
    while y > 0:
        if (y & 1) == 1:
            res = (res * x) % p
        y = y >> 1
        x = (x * x) % p
    return res

def main():
    input_line = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
    st = input_line.split()
    N = int(st[0])
    M = int(st[1])
    L = int(st[2])
    R = int(st[3])
    
    if (N * M) % 2 == 1:
        temp = N * M
        base = R - L + 1
        res = pow(base, temp, MOD)
        print((res + MOD) % MOD)
    else:
        temp = N * M
        base = R - L + 1
        res = pow(base, temp, MOD)
        if (R - L) % 2 == 0:
            res += 1
        res = (res * power(2, MOD - 2, MOD)) % MOD
        print(res)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import math
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data:
        return
    
    n = int(data[0])
    if n > 11:
        print(0)
        return
    
    arr = []
    index = 1
    for i in range(n):
        point = []
        for j in range(5):
            point.append(int(data[index]))
            index += 1
        arr.append(point)
    
    result = []
    
    for i in range(n):
        good = True
        for j in range(n):
            if j == i:
                continue
            for k in range(j + 1, n):
                if k == i:
                    continue
                # Vector from i to j
                v1 = [arr[i][p] - arr[j][p] for p in range(5)]
                # Vector from i to k
                v2 = [arr[i][p] - arr[k][p] for p in range(5)]
                
                # Calculate dot product
                dot_product = sum(v1[p] * v2[p] for p in range(5))
                
                # Calculate magnitudes
                mag1 = math.sqrt(sum(v1[p] ** 2 for p in range(5)))
                mag2 = math.sqrt(sum(v2[p] ** 2 for p in range(5)))
                
                # Avoid division by zero
                if mag1 == 0 or mag2 == 0:
                    continue
                
                # Calculate angle using acos
                cos_angle = dot_product / (mag1 * mag2)
                # Clamp to [-1, 1] to avoid numerical issues
                cos_angle = max(-1, min(1, cos_angle))
                angle = math.acos(cos_angle)
                
                # Check if angle is less than pi/2 - epsilon
                if angle < math.pi / 2 - 1e-9:
                    good = False
                    break
            if not good:
                break
        
        if good:
            result.append(i + 1)
    
    print(len(result))
    for i in result:
        print(i)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: Modern text editors usually show some information regarding the document being edited. For example, the number of words, the number of pages, or the number of characters.In this problem you should implement the similar functionality.You are given a string which only consists of:  uppercase and lowercase English letters,  underscore symbols (they are used as separators),  parentheses (both opening and closing). It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 255) — the length of the given string. The second line contains the string consisting of only lowercase and uppercase English letters, parentheses and underscore symbols.
problem_description.output_spec: Print two space-separated integers:   the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the words "Hello", "Vasya" and "bye" are outside any of the parentheses, and the words "and", "Petya", "and" and "OK" are inside. Note, that the word "and" is given twice and you should count it twice in the answer.

problem_description.description: Modern text editors usually show some information regarding the document being edited. For example, the number of words, the number of pages, or the number of characters.In this problem you should implement the similar functionality.You are given a string which only consists of:  uppercase and lowercase English letters,  underscore symbols (they are used as separators),  parentheses (both opening and closing). It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).

import sys

def countValidParens(s):
    s = re.sub(r'__+', '_', s)
    count = 0
    paren_pattern = re.compile(r'\(([^)]*)\)')
    for match in paren_pattern.finditer(s):
        content = match.group(1)
        if content == '':
            count += 1
        elif '_' not in content:
            count += 1
        else:
            parts = content.split('_')
            nonEmpty = sum(1 for part in parts if part != '')
            count += nonEmpty
    s = re.sub(r'\([^)]*\)', '_', s)
    return count

def findLongestSegment(s):
    s = re.sub(r'__+', '_', s)
    s = re.sub(r'\([^)]*\)', '_', s)
    maxLen = 0
    parts = s.split('_')
    for part in parts:
        if len(part) > maxLen:
            maxLen = len(part)
    return maxLen

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    if len(data) < 2:
        return
    
    n = int(data[0].strip())
    input_str = data[1]
    
    # Split by pattern: parentheses with word characters or underscores inside
    import re
    parts = re.split(r'\([\w_]*\)', input_str)
    
    # Calculate max length of segments between underscores in each part
    max_len = 0
    for s in parts:
        segments = s.split('_')
        if segments:
            current_max = max(len(seg) for seg in segments)
            max_len = max(max_len, current_max)
    
    # Count underscores inside parentheses
    underscore_count = 0
    start = 0
    while True:
        start = input_str.find('(', start)
        if start == -1:
            break
        end = input_str.find(')', start)
        if end == -1:
            break
        inside = input_str[start + 1:end]
        underscore_count += len([s for s in inside.split('_') if s])
        start = end + 1
    
    print(f"{max_len} {underscore_count}")

import re

def main():

import sys

def process():
    input_lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    test_cases = int(input_lines[0].strip())
    
    output_lines = []
    case_num = 1
    index = 1
    
    while case_num <= test_cases and index < len(input_lines):
        line = input_lines[index].strip()
        index += 1
        
        space_index = line.find(' ')
        N = int(line[:space_index])
        input_str = line[space_index + 1:]
        chars = list(input_str)
        
        current_len = 0
        in_paren = 0
        words_in_paren = 0
        longest_seq = 0
        
        for ch in chars:
            if ch == '_':
                if in_paren == 0:
                    longest_seq = max(longest_seq, current_len)
                elif current_len > 0:
                    words_in_paren += 1
                current_len = 0
            elif ch == '(':
                in_paren = 1
                longest_seq = max(longest_seq, current_len)
                current_len = 0
            elif ch == ')':
                in_paren = 0
                if current_len > 0:
                    words_in_paren += 1
                current_len = 0
            else:
                current_len += 1
            
            if in_paren == 0:
                longest_seq = max(longest_seq, current_len)
        
        output_lines.append(f"{longest_seq} {words_in_paren}")
        case_num += 1
    
    print("\n".join(output_lines))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    process()

problem_description.description: Modern text editors usually show some information regarding the document being edited. For example, the number of words, the number of pages, or the number of characters.In this problem you should implement the similar functionality.You are given a string which only consists of:  uppercase and lowercase English letters,  underscore symbols (they are used as separators),  parentheses (both opening and closing). It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 255) — the length of the given string. The second line contains the string consisting of only lowercase and uppercase English letters, parentheses and underscore symbols.
problem_description.output_spec: Print two space-separated integers:   the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the words "Hello", "Vasya" and "bye" are outside any of the parentheses, and the words "and", "Petya", "and" and "OK" are inside. Note, that the word "and" is given twice and you should count it twice in the answer.

import java.util.*;
import java.io.*;

public class Ideone {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        int n = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine());
        String a = br.readLine();
        
        boolean inParentheses = false;
        int maxLen = 0;
        int underscoreSegments = 0;
        int currentLen = 0;
        
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            char c = a.charAt(i);
            if (c == '_') {
                if (inParentheses && currentLen > 0) {
                    underscoreSegments++;
                    currentLen = 0;
                } else {
                    if (currentLen > maxLen) maxLen = currentLen;
                    currentLen = 0;
                }
            } else if (c == '(') {
                inParentheses = true;
                if (currentLen > maxLen) maxLen = currentLen;
                currentLen = 0;
            } else if (c == ')') {
                inParentheses = false;
                if (currentLen > 0) {
                    underscoreSegments++;
                    currentLen = 0;
                }
            } else {
                currentLen++;
            }
        }
        if (currentLen > maxLen) maxLen = currentLen;
        
        System.out.println(maxLen + " " + underscoreSegments);
    }
}

It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).

problem_description.description: Modern text editors usually show some information regarding the document being edited. For example, the number of words, the number of pages, or the number of characters.In this problem you should implement the similar functionality.You are given a string which only consists of:  uppercase and lowercase English letters,  underscore symbols (they are used as separators),  parentheses (both opening and closing). It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 255) — the length of the given string. The second line contains the string consisting of only lowercase and uppercase English letters, parentheses and underscore symbols.
problem_description.output_spec: Print two space-separated integers:   the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the words "Hello", "Vasya" and "bye" are outside any of the parentheses, and the words "and", "Petya", "and" and "OK" are inside. Note, that the word "and" is given twice and you should count it twice in the answer.

problem_description.description: Modern text editors usually show some information regarding the document being edited. For example, the number of words, the number of pages, or the number of characters.In this problem you should implement the similar functionality.You are given a string which only consists of:  uppercase and lowercase English letters,  underscore symbols (they are used as separators),  parentheses (both opening and closing). It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).

import re

def main():
    n = int(input())
    s = input().strip()
    
    regex = r"\([a-zA-Z_]*\)"
    pat = re.compile(regex)
    new_string = pat.sub("_", s)
    
    left = re.split(r"_+", new_string)
    max_length = 0
    for i in range(len(left)):
        max_length = max(max_length, len(left[i]))
    
    print(max_length)
    
    count = 0
    is_start = False
    start_index = -1
    end_index = -1
    
    for i in range(len(s)):
        c = s[i]
        if c == '(':
            is_start = True
            start_index = i
            continue
        if is_start:
            if c == ')':
                is_start = False
                end_index = i
                tmp = s[start_index+1:end_index]
                if tmp == "":
                    continue
                if tmp.startswith("_"):
                    tmps = re.split(r"_+", tmp)
                    if len(tmps) != 0:
                        count += (len(tmps) - 1)
                    else:
                        count += len(tmps)
                else:
                    tmps = re.split(r"_+", tmp)
                    count += len(tmps)
    
    print(count)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    if not data:
        return
    
    n = int(data[0].strip())
    s = data[1].strip()
    
    # Replace parentheses and their contents with underscores
    sb = []
    inside = False
    for c in s:
        if c == '(':
            inside = True
            sb.append('_')

            inside = False
            sb.append('_')

    inside = False
    current = []
    for c in s:

import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    if not data:
        return
    n = int(data[0].strip())
    s = data[1].strip()
    
    # Replace content inside parentheses with underscores
    sb = []
    depth = 0
    for c in s:
        if c == '(':
            depth += 1
            sb.append('_')
        elif c == ')':
            depth -= 1
            sb.append('_')
        elif depth > 0:
            sb.append('_')
        else:
            sb.append(c)
    
    processed = ''.join(sb)
    tokens = processed.split('_')
    # Filter out empty strings
    tokens = [t for t in tokens if t]
    max_len = max((len(t) for t in tokens), default=0)
    
    print(max_len)
    
    # Count underscore-separated segments inside parentheses
    cnt = 0
    depth = 0
    inside = []
    for c in s:
        if c == '(':
            depth += 1
            inside = []
        elif c == ')':
            if depth > 0:
                content = ''.join(inside)
                if content:
                    segs = content.split('_')
                    segs = [s for s in segs if s]
                    cnt += len(segs)
            depth -= 1
        elif depth > 0:
            inside.append(c)
    
    print(cnt)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys

def ak375(n, s):
    tmpstr2 = []
    tmpstr1 = []
    i = 0
    
    while i < n:
        if s[i] == '(':
            tmpstr2.append("_")
            i += 1
            while i < n and s[i] != ')':
                tmpstr2.append(s[i])
                i += 1
        elif s[i] == ')':
            tmpstr1.append("_")
        else:
            tmpstr1.append(s[i])
        i += 1
    
    tmpstr2_joined = ''.join(tmpstr2)
    arrstr2 = [part for part in tmpstr2_joined.split('_') if part]
    res2 = len(arrstr2)
    
    tmpstr1_joined = ''.join(tmpstr1)
    arrstr1 = tmpstr1_joined.split('_')
    res1 = max((len(part) for part in arrstr1), default=0)
    
    return f"{res1} {res2}"

def main():
    input_data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    idx = 0
    results = []
    while idx < len(input_data):
        n = int(input_data[idx])
        idx += 1
        s = input_data[idx]
        idx += 1
        res = ak375(n, s)
        results.append(res)
    
    for res in results:
        print(res)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: Modern text editors usually show some information regarding the document being edited. For example, the number of words, the number of pages, or the number of characters.In this problem you should implement the similar functionality.You are given a string which only consists of:  uppercase and lowercase English letters,  underscore symbols (they are used as separators),  parentheses (both opening and closing). It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 255) — the length of the given string. The second line contains the string consisting of only lowercase and uppercase English letters, parentheses and underscore symbols.
problem_description.output_spec: Print two space-separated integers:   the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the words "Hello", "Vasya" and "bye" are outside any of the parentheses, and the words "and", "Petya", "and" and "OK" are inside. Note, that the word "and" is given twice and you should count it twice in the answer.

import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class Main {

    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
        int n = sc.nextInt();
        String s = sc.next();

        int countMax = 0;
        int countNoInside = 0;
        int currentWordLength = 0;
        boolean inBrackets = false;

        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
            char ch = s.charAt(i);

            if (ch == '(') {
                countMax = Math.max(countMax, currentWordLength);
                currentWordLength = 0;
                inBrackets = true;
            } else if (ch == ')') {
                if (currentWordLength > 0) {
                    countNoInside++;
                }
                currentWordLength = 0;
                inBrackets = false;
            } else if (ch == '_') {
                if (inBrackets) {
                    if (currentWordLength > 0) {
                        countNoInside++;
                    }
                } else {
                    countMax = Math.max(countMax, currentWordLength);
                }
                currentWordLength = 0;
            } else {
                currentWordLength++;
            }
        }

        countMax = Math.max(countMax, currentWordLength);
        System.out.println(countMax + " " + countNoInside);
    }

    static class Scanner {
        private BufferedReader reader;
        private StringTokenizer tokenizer;

        public Scanner(InputStream input) {
            reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(input));
        }

        public Scanner(FileReader reader) {
            this.reader = new BufferedReader(reader);
        }

        public String next() throws IOException {
            while (tokenizer == null || !tokenizer.hasMoreTokens()) {
                tokenizer = new StringTokenizer(reader.readLine());
            }
            return tokenizer.nextToken();
        }

        public int nextInt() throws IOException {
            return Integer.parseInt(next());
        }

        public long nextLong() throws IOException {
            return Long.parseLong(next());

        public String nextLine() throws IOException {
            return reader.readLine();
        }

        }

        public boolean ready() throws IOException {
            return reader.ready();
        }
    }
}

import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    if not data:
        return
    
    # First line contains an integer to consume
    # Second line contains the string input
    if len(data) > 1:
        input_str = data[1].strip()
    else:
        # If only one line, assume it's the integer line and there's no string
        input_str = ""
    
    maxLength = 0
    currentLength = 0
    wordCounter = 0
    insideParens = False
    lastCharWasAlpha = False

    for idx in range(len(input_str)):
        ch = input_str[idx]
        isAlphabetic = ch.isalpha()

        if isAlphabetic:
            if insideParens and not lastCharWasAlpha:
                wordCounter += 1
            if not insideParens:
                currentLength += 1
            maxLength = max(maxLength, currentLength)
            lastCharWasAlpha = True
        elif ch == '_':
            lastCharWasAlpha = False
            maxLength = max(maxLength, currentLength)
            currentLength = 0
        elif ch == '(':
            lastCharWasAlpha = False
            insideParens = True
            maxLength = max(maxLength, currentLength)
            currentLength = 0
        elif ch == ')':
            insideParens = False
            lastCharWasAlpha = False
            maxLength = max(maxLength, currentLength)
            currentLength = 0

    print(f"{maxLength} {wordCounter}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read
    st = input().strip()
    
    in_list = []
    i = 0
    cnt = 0
    j = 0
    maxl = 0
    
    while i < st.rfind(')'):
        # Find next '(' after position i
        open_pos = st.find('(', i)
        if open_pos == -1:
            break
            
        # Extract substring from j to before next '('
        s = st[j:open_pos]
        
        # Process tokens separated by '_'
        tokens = s.split('_')
        for token in tokens:
            l = len(token)
            if l > maxl:
                maxl = l
        
        # Find next ')' after j
        close_pos = st.find(')', j + 1)
        if close_pos == -1:
            break
            
        j = close_pos + 1
        
        # Extract substring inside parentheses
        inside = st[open_pos + 1:close_pos]
        
        # Process tokens inside parentheses
        inside_tokens = inside.split('_')
        for token in inside_tokens:
            if token != "":
                cnt += 1
        
        i = close_pos
    
    # Process remaining substring after last ')'
    s = st[j:]
    tokens = s.split('_')
    for token in tokens:
        l = len(token)
        if l > maxl:
            maxl = l
    
    print(f"{maxl} {cnt}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from functools import partial

def processSegment(s, consumer):
    for token in s.split("_"):
        consumer(len(token))

def processInner(s, consumer):
    for token in s.split("_"):
        consumer(token)

def main():
    lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    if len(lines) < 2:
        return
    
    input_str = lines[1]
    
    maxLength = 0
    innerCount = 0
    segmentStart = 0

    i = 0
    while i < len(input_str):
        if input_str[i] == '(':
            segment = input_str[segmentStart:i]

            closeIndex = input_str.find(')', i)
            if closeIndex == -1:

            inner = input_str[i+1:closeIndex]
            processInner(inner, lambda token: globals().update({'innerCount': globals()['innerCount'] + 1}) if token else None)
            
            segmentStart = closeIndex + 1
            i = closeIndex
        i += 1
    
    finalSegment = input_str[segmentStart:]
    processSegment(finalSegment, lambda len_val: globals().update({'maxLength': max(globals()['maxLength'], len_val)}) if True else None)

problem_description.description: Modern text editors usually show some information regarding the document being edited. For example, the number of words, the number of pages, or the number of characters.In this problem you should implement the similar functionality.You are given a string which only consists of:  uppercase and lowercase English letters,  underscore symbols (they are used as separators),  parentheses (both opening and closing). It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 255) — the length of the given string. The second line contains the string consisting of only lowercase and uppercase English letters, parentheses and underscore symbols.
problem_description.output_spec: Print two space-separated integers:   the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the words "Hello", "Vasya" and "bye" are outside any of the parentheses, and the words "and", "Petya", "and" and "OK" are inside. Note, that the word "and" is given twice and you should count it twice in the answer.

        String s = sc.nextLine();
        s = sc.nextLine();
        
        // Extract content inside parentheses
        StringBuilder insideParens = new StringBuilder();
        int flag = 0;
        for (char c : s.toCharArray()) {
            if (c == '(') flag = 1;
            else if (c == ')') {
                insideParens.append(' ');
                flag = 0;
            } else if (flag == 1) {
                insideParens.append(c);
            }
        }
        
        // Remove parentheses and their contents
        StringBuilder outsideParens = new StringBuilder();

        while (true) {
            int open = s.indexOf('(', start);
            if (open == -1) {
                outsideParens.append(s.substring(start));
                break;
            }
            int close = s.indexOf(')', open);
            if (close == -1) {
                outsideParens.append(s.substring(start));
                break;
            }
            outsideParens.append(s, start, open).append(' ');
            start = close + 1;

problem_description.description: Modern text editors usually show some information regarding the document being edited. It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).

problem_description.description: Modern text editors usually show some information regarding the document being edited. For example, the number of words, the number of pages, or the number of characters.In this problem you should implement the similar functionality.You are given a string which only consists of:  uppercase and lowercase English letters,  underscore symbols (they are used as separators),  parentheses (both opening and closing). It is guaranteed that each opening parenthesis has a succeeding closing parenthesis. Similarly, each closing parentheses has a preceding opening parentheses matching it. For each pair of matching parentheses there are no other parenthesis between them. In other words, each parenthesis in the string belongs to a matching "opening-closing" pair, and such pairs can't be nested.For example, the following string is valid: "_Hello_Vasya(and_Petya)__bye_(and_OK)".Word is a maximal sequence of consecutive letters, i.e. such sequence that the first character to the left and the first character to the right of it is an underscore, a parenthesis, or it just does not exist. For example, the string above consists of seven words: "Hello", "Vasya", "and", "Petya", "bye", "and" and "OK". Write a program that finds:  the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 255) — the length of the given string. The second line contains the string consisting of only lowercase and uppercase English letters, parentheses and underscore symbols.
problem_description.output_spec: Print two space-separated integers:   the length of the longest word outside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word outside the parentheses),  the number of words inside the parentheses (print 0, if there is no word inside the parentheses).
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first sample, the words "Hello", "Vasya" and "bye" are outside any of the parentheses, and the words "and", "Petya", "and" and "OK" are inside. Note, that the word "and" is given twice and you should count it twice in the answer.

problem_description.description: One day Greg and his friends were walking in the forest. Overall there were n people walking, including Greg. Soon he found himself in front of a river. The guys immediately decided to get across the river. Luckily, there was a boat by the river bank, just where the guys were standing. We know that the boat can hold people with the total weight of at most k kilograms.Greg immediately took a piece of paper and listed there the weights of all people in his group (including himself). It turned out that each person weights either 50 or 100 kilograms. Now Greg wants to know what minimum number of times the boat needs to cross the river to transport the whole group to the other bank. The boat needs at least one person to navigate it from one bank to the other. As the boat crosses the river, it can have any non-zero number of passengers as long as their total weight doesn't exceed k.Also Greg is wondering, how many ways there are to transport everybody to the other side in the minimum number of boat rides. Two ways are considered distinct if during some ride they have distinct sets of people on the boat.Help Greg with this problem.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line contains two integers n, k (1 ≤ n ≤ 50, 1 ≤ k ≤ 5000) — the number of people, including Greg, and the boat's weight limit. The next line contains n integers — the people's weights. A person's weight is either 50 kilos or 100 kilos. You can consider Greg and his friends indexed in some way.
problem_description.output_spec: In the first line print an integer — the minimum number of rides. If transporting everyone to the other bank is impossible, print an integer -1. In the second line print the remainder after dividing the number of ways to transport the people in the minimum number of rides by number 1000000007 (109 + 7). If transporting everyone to the other bank is impossible, print integer 0.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first test Greg walks alone and consequently, he needs only one ride across the river.In the second test you should follow the plan:  transport two 50 kg. people;  transport one 50 kg. person back;  transport one 100 kg. person;  transport one 50 kg. person back;  transport two 50 kg. people. That totals to 5 rides. Depending on which person to choose at step 2, we can get two distinct ways.

import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class Main {
    static final long MOD = 1_000_000_007L;

    long modExp(long b, long e) {
        long r = 1;
        b %= MOD;
        while (e > 0) {
            if ((e & 1) == 1) r = (r * b) % MOD;
            b = (b * b) % MOD;
            e >>>= 1;
        }
        return r;
    }

    long modInv(long x) {
        return modExp(x, MOD - 2);
    }

    void solve() {
        long[] f = new long[51];
        f[0] = 1;
        for (int i = 1; i <= 50; i++) f[i] = (f[i-1] * i) % MOD;

        long[][] comb = new long[51][51];
        for (int i = 0; i <= 50; i++) {
            comb[i][0] = 1;
            for (int j = 1; j <= i; j++) {
                long d = (f[j] * f[i-j]) % MOD;
                comb[i][j] = (f[i] * modInv(d)) % MOD;
            }
        }

        int N = ni(), K = ni();
        int cnt50 = 0, cnt100 = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
            int v = ni();
            if (v == 100) cnt100++;
            else cnt50++;
        }

        Vertex[][][] V = new Vertex[cnt50+1][cnt100+1][2];
        for (int a = 0; a <= cnt50; a++) {
            for (int b = 0; b <= cnt100; b++) {
                V[a][b][0] = new Vertex(a, b, 0);
                V[a][b][1] = new Vertex(a, b, 1);
            }
        }

        for (int a = 0; a <= cnt50; a++) {
            for (int b = 0; b <= cnt100; b++) {
                int maxBills50 = Math.min(K / 50, a);
                int maxBills100 = Math.min(K / 100, b);
                for (int h = maxBills100; h >= 0; h--) {
                    int rem = K - 100 * h;
                    int maxFiftyUse = Math.min(maxBills50, rem / 50);
                    for (int f = maxFiftyUse; f >= 0; f--) {
                        if (f == 0 && h == 0) continue;
                        Vertex u = V[a][b][0];
                        Vertex v = V[a-f][b-h][1];
                        u.out.add(v);
                        v.out.add(u);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        ArrayDeque<Vertex> Q = new ArrayDeque<>();
        V[cnt50][cnt100][0].depth = 1;
        V[cnt50][cnt100][0].ways = 1;
        Q.add(V[cnt50][cnt100][0]);

        while (!Q.isEmpty()) {
            Vertex cur = Q.remove();
            for (Vertex next : cur.out) {
                if (next.depth == 0 || next.depth == cur.depth + 1) {
                    int fiveFrom = cur.flag == 0 ? cur.five : cnt50 - cur.five;
                    int fiveToUse = Math.abs(cur.five - next.five);
                    long c1 = comb[fiveFrom][fiveToUse];

                    int hundredFrom = cur.flag == 0 ? cur.hundred : cnt100 - cur.hundred;
                    int hundredToUse = Math.abs(cur.hundred - next.hundred);
                    long c2 = comb[hundredFrom][hundredToUse];

                    long edgeWays = (c1 * c2) % MOD;
                    next.ways = (next.ways + (cur.ways * edgeWays) % MOD) % MOD;

                    if (next.depth == 0) {
                        next.depth = cur.depth + 1;
                        Q.add(next);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        Vertex sink = V[0][0][1];
        System.out.println((sink.depth - 1) + "\n" + sink.ways);
    }

    static class Vertex {

MOD = 1_000_000_007

def mod_exp(b, e):

    while e > 0:

            r = (r * b) % MOD
        b = (b * b) % MOD

    return r

            max_bills_100 = min(K // 100, b)
            for h in range(max_bills_100, -1, -1):

                max_fifty_use = min(max_bills_50, rem // 50)
                for f_val in range(max_fifty_use, -1, -1):
